term3._source: Term 3 week specs og_planner/weeks/term3_week1-10.json. Week 10 reviewed all 18 words and taught none.
_corrections: tongue: Week 1 highlighted ongue, Week 2 highlighted ue. Settled on ongue - both the o saying /u/ and the silent ue are unfair.
asthma: Week 9 notes said AST-muh, but the t is not pronounced. Correct Australian pronunciation is AS-muh.

words.why: the c is silent, so sc just says /s/; you hear the c as /k/ in muscular
the o says /u/ and the ue is silent, so gue just says /g/
ough says /ow/ here, but /uff/ in enough and /oh/ in though
uoy says /oy/; English almost never puts those letters in that order
after the c, ui says a short /i/
ts says /s/ because the word kept its Japanese spelling
ou says /uh/ and the French -age says /ahzh/
ei says long /i/ (Greek seis); graph is the same ending as pictograph
ci says /sh/ and es says /eez/; one species, ten species
Greek ch says /k/ and the a says /uh/
the r is silent and the o says /uh/; you hear the r in ironic
eo says one short /e/ and ard says /uhd/
au says long /ay/ here, not the /or/ of caught
two u letters in a row, saying /yoo/ then /uh/
the l is silent, exactly like salmon
the th in the middle is silent
y is the only vowel letter and says a short /i/; the h behind the r is silent

term3._source: Term 3 week specs. class_language is the wording students met - reuse it in later review.

weeks.class_language: a preposition tells where, when or direction; the phrase includes its whole noun group

weeks.focus: Identify adverbials and switch them to the front and back
weeks.class_language: an adverbial tells when, where, how or why; a fronted adverbial takes a comma
comma only when the detail is at the front
a clause has its own verb, a phrase does not; a main clause stands alone, a subordinate clause leaves you waiting
an appositive renames the noun beside it, inside two commas; cover it and the sentence still works

weeks.focus: Differentiate between simple, compound and complex sentences
weeks.class_language: Sentence Smackdown signals - one finger stands alone, a fist leaves you waiting, two fingers compound; hand chop at the split

weeks.focus: Identify main and subordinate clauses and the subordinating conjunction
weeks.class_language: labels M, S and T; T is the trigger word; a fronted S takes a comma

weeks.focus: Use nominalisation for variety, objectivity and an impersonal tone
weeks.class_language: action word -> thing word; the person steps out; word bank -ence -ance -cy -ice -ity -acy

weeks.focus: Define acronym, recall common acronyms, use brackets to expand one
weeks.class_language: full name first, short form in round brackets, then the short form alone; initialisms treated as acronyms
Tue prepositional phrases + adverbials; Wed phrase, clause + appositive; Thu simple/compound/complex + trigger word; Fri nominalisation + acronyms (no Monday session)

term3.labels_used: preposition and noun group (Week 1), verb (from Week 4), subordinating conjunction (Weeks 6-7), noun and verb (Week 8). adjective and adverb were never taught as labels - keep them out of questions outside the grammar section (section 2b).
